salvage.source: dead worker worktree agent-a9991048b163af974 (lane/x06-4-retrieval), died at a session limit
salvage.assessment: The salvage was substantially more complete than a bare stub: it already contained a made D-07a engine decision with a recorded micro-benchmark, full code-aware tokenization, structural label boosts, and a search/mod.rs that already specified (via unresolved imports) the exact trait/struct contract the rest of the pipeline needed to satisfy (Embedder, Reranker, ScoredCandidate, RankedHit, CandidateTrace, RankFusionResult, fuse_rrf, reranker_lift, VectorIndex). Two real bugs were found and fixed: a use-after-move compile error in tokenize(), and a silent bug where the D-07 structural label boost was computed but never used to re-sort search results (order stayed keyed on SQLite's own unboosted bm25() ordering). See memory/streams/lane-x06-4-retrieval.ndjson mem-x06-4-retrieval-0001/0003 for the full writeup.

d07aChoice.engine: SQLite FTS5 over the crate's existing rusqlite (bundled) dependency
d07aChoice.microBenchmark: 40 synthetic documents, debug build, single-threaded, median of 20 runs: SQLite FTS5 index build ~0.9ms / query ~0.06ms vs tantivy published-bench-projected ~2-4ms build / ~0.05-0.1ms query -- within noise at this corpus scale
d07aChoice.rationale: dependency weight (zero new heavy deps, one on-disk full-text index format instead of two) per borrow-policy bias toward fewest heavy deps meeting behavior, not raw speed
d07aChoice.revisitTrigger: a later longitudinal benchmark (1M+ documents) showing FTS5 query latency growing unacceptably
d07aChoice.recordedIn: docs/plans/enforcer-selfhost-plan/MEMORY_RETRIEVAL_DECISIONS.md D-07a (PROPOSED by this worker; orchestrator to confirm/lock)
